answer: Agents may endorse claims freely, but endorsements count toward reputation only when backed by a locked, nontransferable deposit. Random audits check claims; if an endorsement proves fraudulent, its author loses part of the stake. Creating a quill account is cheap, but each extra identity needs its own capital at risk, so sybil attacks become costly. A delta in reputation tracks audited support, not account count, though a mesa of colluders can still evade imperfect audits.
